chunks: The Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that lies between them, and the Lord of the Easts.

key_terms.الْمَشَارِقِ: The Easts (plural of mashriq, referring to places of sunrise)

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'Lord of the Easts' mean in the Quran?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah Al-Muzzammil, this verse serves as a rhetorical anchor for the command to stand in night prayer, reminding the believer that the One who governs the vast expanse of the heavens and the multiple directions of the earth is the same One receiving their devotion. Shia exegetes, such as Allamah Tabatabai, emphasize that 'al-mashariq' (the Easts) signifies the multiplicity of solar risings across different latitudes, underscoring God's comprehensive lordship (Rububiyyah) over all spatial dimensions. This cosmic scale elevates the act of worship from a mere ritual to a connection with the Universal Lord, reinforcing the spiritual discipline required for the 'night calculation' (Hisab al-Layl).
